questions.stem: The Apatani tribe, famous for their nose-plug tradition and sustainable rice-fish farming, inhabits which state?
questions.explanation: The Apatani (or Tanw) live in the Ziro Valley of Lower Subansiri district, Arunachal Pradesh. Famous for: (1) the facial 'Yapping Hulo' tradition (now discontinued — older Apatani women had large nose plugs and facial tattoos, done historically to make them 'unattractive' to raiding tribes); (2) sustainable wet-rice and fish (paddy-cum-pisciculture) farming on valley floors without using any animal power or wheel — a UNESCO candidate site for cultural landscape; (3) the Dree festival (July). The Apatani language belongs to the Tani branch of Sino-Tibetan.

questions.stem: The Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo are the three major indigenous tribes of which state?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya ('abode of clouds') has three major tribes inhabiting three hill regions: KHASI (central Khasi Hills — language is Khasian, an Austroasiatic language unique in NE), JAINTIA (eastern Jaintia Hills), and GARO (western Garo Hills — Tibeto-Burman language). All three are MATRILINEAL societies (inheritance through the mother's line — one of the largest surviving matrilineal societies in the world). The Khasis and Jaintias consider themselves 'Hynñiewtrep' (seven huts); the Garos call themselves 'A·chik'.

questions.stem: The term PVTG (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group) was introduced in India during which period, and how many PVTGs are officially recognised?
questions.explanation: PVTGs were first recognised in 1975 (under the Dhebar Commission recommendation) as 'Primitive Tribal Groups' (PTGs); renamed PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUPS in 2006. Currently 75 PVTGs are officially listed across 18 states + A&N Islands. Criteria for PVTG status: (a) pre-agricultural technology; (b) stagnant/declining population; (c) low literacy; (d) economic backwardness. Odisha has the MOST PVTGs (13), followed by Andhra Pradesh. Among PVTGs: Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese (all A&N); Birhor, Saura, Korwa; Chenchu (AP); Toda (TN); Bhil-Koli; Sahariya.

questions.stem: The Toda tribe, known for their distinctive barrel-vaulted huts and buffalo-centric culture, inhabits which hill region?
questions.explanation: The Toda (or Todar) are a small pastoral community of the Nilgiri Hills (Tamil Nadu), famous for: (1) half-barrel 'munds' (thatched huts without doors or windows; entry through a small opening); (2) sacred buffalo-based culture and associated dairy rituals; (3) intricate embroidered 'Pugur' shawls (GI-tagged). Population is tiny (~1500). Recognised as a PVTG. The Badaga, Kota, Irula, and Kurumba also inhabit the Nilgiris — studied extensively by anthropologists.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Sentinelese, one of the world's last uncontacted tribes, inhabit which island?
questions.explanation: The Sentinelese live on North Sentinel Island (Andaman & Nicobar Islands). One of the world's last uncontacted peoples — they hostilely reject all outside contact. The Indian government protects them under the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (PATR) Regulation, 1956, which prohibits approach within 5 km of the island. Population: ~50-100 (estimated). Speak a language unrelated to any other known; classified a PVTG. Other Andaman PVTGs: Jarawa (South & Middle Andaman), Onge (Little Andaman), Great Andamanese (Strait Island). Shompen (Great Nicobar) is a Nicobarese PVTG.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Bhil tribe, one of India's largest tribal communities, is primarily concentrated in which states?
questions.explanation: The Bhil are India's third-largest tribe (after Gonds and Santhals), concentrated in the Aravalli-Vindhya-Satpura region — MP, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and parts of Tripura. Historically known as fierce archers (the Mahabharata mentions Eklavya as a Bhil prince). Bhil Pithora paintings are their cultural art. Famous Bhil personalities: Jhalkari Bai (Rani of Jhansi's general), Tantya Bhil (freedom fighter, called 'Indian Robin Hood'). Largest Indian tribes by population (2011 Census): 1. Gond, 2. Santhal (Santal), 3. Bhil, 4. Mina, 5. Oraon.

questions.stem: The Konyak Nagas, formerly known for the now-extinct practice of headhunting, primarily inhabit which region?
questions.explanation: The Konyaks are the largest Naga tribe, concentrated in Mon district, northern Nagaland, straddling the Myanmar border. Until the mid-20th c., Konyaks were feared headhunters; the practice ended in the 1960s after Christianisation. Distinctive features: elaborate face tattoos (historically marking successful warriors), pipe smoking by both genders, brass skulls on necklaces. Their festival is AOLING (spring). Major Naga tribes (17 officially): Angami, Ao, Chakhesang, Chang, Konyak, Lotha, Phom, Pochury, Rengma, Sangtam, Sema (Sumi), Yimchungru, Zeliang, Khiamniungan, Kuki, Kachari, Garo.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Gond tribe, India's largest tribal community, primarily speaks which language family?
questions.explanation: The Gonds are India's largest tribe (population ~13 million per 2011 Census) — primarily in MP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, AP, Odisha. Their language GONDI belongs to the Dravidian family (not Indo-Aryan, despite the central-Indian geography) — a reminder that Dravidian languages once extended much further north than today. Gondwana region is named after them. Ruled several kingdoms between the 10th-18th c. (Gond Kingdoms of Garha Katanga, Chanda, Deogarh, Mandla). Famous Gond queen: Rani Durgavati of Gondwana (d. 1564 fighting Akbar).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Santhals, India's second-largest tribe, speak a language belonging to which family?
questions.explanation: The Santhals (or Santal) speak Santali, an Austroasiatic language of the Munda branch — one of India's oldest language families, surviving only in pockets (Santali, Mundari, Ho, Kharia, Kurku, Khasi). Santali was added to the 8th Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003). Uses the OL CHIKI script (invented by Pandit Raghunath Murmu in 1925). Largest concentration: Jharkhand, WB, Odisha, Bihar. Famous Santhal leaders: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (led the 1855 Santhal Rebellion / 'Santhal Hul' against British and zamindars). Santhal Hul Day: 30 June.

questions.stem: The Jarawa and Onge tribes are PVTGs inhabiting which islands?
questions.explanation: JARAWAS live in the western forested areas of Middle and South Andaman; population ~400 (2011) — up from a low of <300 in the 1990s. Recognised a PVTG. Historically hostile to outsiders until a peaceful contact breakthrough in 1998. ONGE live on Little Andaman; population ~120 — a declining PVTG. They are hunter-gatherers. All four 'Negrito' Andamanese tribes (Great Andamanese, Jarawa, Onge, Sentinelese) speak related languages unrelated to any mainland language. Nicobarese (Shompen, Nicobarese) are Mongoloid and ethnically/linguistically distinct from Andamanese.
